title.narrative: Bangladesh Sustainable Coastal and Marine Fisheries

description.narrative: The objective of the Sustainable Coastal and Marine Fisheries Project is to increase coastal and marine fisheries contribution to the economy, poverty reduction, and environmental stability. The proposed PDO of the first project under the series (phase one) is to improve management of coastal and marine fisheries and aquaculture. There are four components to the project, the first component being Enabling Activities for Sustainable Fisheries Sector Investments and Growth. Component one supports the GOB commitment to sustainably develop the country's enlarged EEZ19 through: (a) more effective management of coastal fisheries, with responsibilities shared between the DOF and artisanal fishing communities; (b) improved sector transparency, integrity, and accountability; and (c) gender-balanced institutional development. This component includes three subcomponents: stock assessment and development of national fishery management plan, enabling investments in sustainable fisheries, and MCS development and IUU fishing reduction. The second component is the improving infrastructure and production practices. This component supports closing of basic infrastructure and technical capacity gaps to promote integrated value chain development and compliance with standards. It will support measures for improving genetic quality, biosecurity, and disease control in shrimp hatcheries that are expected to significantly reduce coastal aquaculture exposure to devastating disease outbreaks and production crashes. This component includes three subcomponents: infrastructure improvements for capture and culture fisheries, value chain and food safety development, and boosting coastal aquaculture productivity. The third component is the community empowerment and livelihoods. The component uses a community-driven development (CDD) approach and a package of investment and financial support aiming at strengthening community fisheries management and transforming livelihoods in poor fishing communities by reducing dependence on fishing. This component includes two subcomponents: fishing community institutions and alternative livelihoods development, and business development and market linkages for alternative livelihoods. Finally, the fourth component is the project management and monitoring.

The series of projects' Development Objective is to increase coastal and marine fisheries contribution to the economy, poverty reduction, and environmental stability.The proposed PDO of the first project under the series (Phase 1) is to improve management of coastal and marine fisheries and aquaculture.

title.narrative: Savings and loans groups (Fishers Groups) created

comment.narrative: Target achieved. - Total 4,500 Savings and Loan Groups have been formed across 450 villages under 45 Upazilas in 13 districts, with an average of 10 groups per village. These groups are fully managed by the community. As of now: • The groups have collectively accumulated BDT 97.5 million through member savings. • They have disbursed BDT 194 million as internal loans from these savings. • 2,236 households have started income-generating activities (IGAs) using their own group savings.

title.narrative: Fisheries Management Plans (FMPs) prepared according to defined criteria and operational

comment.narrative: Target achieved. 3 FMPs have been approved and are under implementation. The fisheries for which management plans were prepared and are being implemented are Industrial Fleet (FMP-1), Artisanal Fleet (FMP-2), and MCS Plan (FMP-3). A JMC was established in Patenga,Chattogram, a JMC-Coordination Committee was formed by MoFL, an MOU was signed among 11 JMC parties in order to ensure coordinated monitoring of fishing activities and prevention of IUU fishing. Stock assessment for 8 species/groups was done in 2023 and report published, , the VMS has been piloting since October 2024, issuance of fishing permits for the artisanal fisheries is on-going, 50 on-board observers have been deployed by the project since June 2024 and have been attached under Director Marine, C&E data are being collected from 175 landing sites through 195 data enumerators, and a fishing vessels and gears database has been developed and updated annually.

title.narrative: Share of landed catch and aquaculture production in targeted coastal belt fisheries in safe handling according to defined criteria

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. - Renovation & rehabilitation of 6 Post-harvest Service Centers completed -Training on behavioral changes on post-harvest handling and preservation techniques conducted (1039 batches, 27550 participants) - Fisheries co-management committee discussed good post-harvest handling techniques -10 Sensitization campaign on fish/shrimp products quality - Construction of 3 Fish Landing Station and 2 Fish Market completed, 5 mini landing centres constructed; Organized 4 workshop/ campaign on Hygiene and Sanitation; and -Provided 2663 Styrofoam Boxes and 1,800 plastic crates for temporary storage and transportation. The total catch from industrial and artisanal fisheries is 628,623 MT, of which 253,535 MT already safely handled (40.60%), aquaculture production from shrimp cluster is 2,852, which is totally safe handled, resulted 100.00% achievement.

title.narrative: Issuance of industrial fishing licenses in line with precautionary principle

comment.narrative: Target achieved. There are more than 100 commercial species harvested from the Bay of Bengal. However, only 10 and 8 species were assessed in 2019 and 2023 respectively and reported in Bangladesh Marine Fish Stock Assessment Reports. Stock status report 2019 revealed slight to severe level of overfishing of 8 stocks out of 10 and report 2023 indicated overall shrimp stock as overfished. Length-frequency and Catch and Effort data provided conflicting results on the status of Hilsa Shad. More recent data has yet to be analyzed. In aforesaid contexts, issuing new fishing license has been stopped since 2019. According to the precautionary approach provision of no issuance of new license is included in fisheries management plan 2021.

title.narrative: Share of households who indicate that more than 50% of their income is coming from outside capture fish.

comment.narrative: A total of 1,063 beneficiaries have received revolving loan support to establish micro-enterprise. The project has supported livelihood diversification by providing training, arranging alternative income-generating activities (AIGAs), and providing community-based financing. These efforts enabled fishers to invest in agriculture, livestock, small businesses, and aquaculture, creating more stable and sustainable income streams. Achievement of the project intervention is that 49.8% of surveyed households earn more than half of their total income beyond capture fisheries.

During this mission the target was reduced from 10 to 5. - Progress 3 FLS–65%, and 2 FM 75% and expected to be completed by August 2025 and will fully functionalized to facilitate safe handling of landed catch.

title.narrative: Aquaculture farmers with access to productivity sustaining or boosting packages

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. A total of 8,900 aquaculture farmers were trained of which 8,750 are shrimp cluster farmers and 150 are neighboring farmers trained and supported under grant window-1 sub projects. All the trained farmers have access to the production boosting packages that include – SPF PL, Good quality feed, prebiotic, probiotic and steady water supply. Moreover, good aquaculture practices and bio-security protocols were maintained by the farmers. Routine water quality and fish health were also monitored throughout the culture cycle. Canal re-excavated, SPF PL stocked, adopted GAP, and climate resilience-leading to boosted production.

title.narrative: Hectares of terrestrial and aquatic areas under enhanced conservation and management

comment.narrative: Note the previous figure will be corrected. The total Bay of Bengal is, 11.8 million hectares, which is fully now underimproved management, with 0.81 million hectares of marine protected areas enhanced. Management measures based on FMPs, NPOA-IUU, and MPA plans have begun. The Joint Monitoring Cell (JMC) monitors fishing activity and MCS implementation. Data collection and fish stock assessments support evidence-based management and conservation. Enhanced MPA plans and strategies boost biodiversity conservation. Strengthening MCS by establishing the JMC, improving vessel monitoring systems, and introducing an observer program has improved conservation.

title.narrative: Share of artisanal vessels with installed and functioning vessel monitoring and communication safety equipment

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. GSM devices have been installed in 8500 artisanal Vessels which is 28.45% against total registered artisanal vessel (29867) and 33.05% against total approved artisanal vessel (25724). Tracking artisanal vessels using these devices revealed that the GSM devices are suitable for small artisanal vessels fishing near-shore. However consistent communication is not possible with inconsistent mobile networks at sea.
